questions.q: What four advanced visualization techniques does this challenge ask you to combine into one dashboard?
options: A dual-axis combination chart, a KPI shape view, a Pareto chart, and a dynamic parameter-driven reference line
Four identical bar charts with different colors
A map, a scatter plot, a pie chart, and a text table
Four separate dashboards, one per chart type
questions.explain: The challenge draws one requirement from each of the previous four lessons: dual-axis (74), KPI (75), Pareto (76), and dynamic reference lines (77) — all combined onto a single dashboard.

questions.q: According to the self-check rubric, what distinguishes a properly built KPI view from one that just looks similar?
options: It uses the Shape mark type driven by a real threshold calculation, not manual coloring
It uses more than ten colors
It has no calculated fields at all
It is built entirely from a table calculation, with no LOD or IF logic
questions.explain: The rubric specifically calls out that a real KPI view is Shape-driven by an actual threshold calculation (like IF SUM([Sales]) > 25000 ...), not just manually colored to look similar.

questions.q: What makes the Pareto chart's cumulative line 'genuine' according to the rubric, rather than faked?
options: It's built from real running total and percent-of-total table calculations computed using Sub-Category, not a manually typed series of numbers
It must be colored bright red
It must be the only mark on the entire dashboard
It requires no dual axis at all
questions.explain: The rubric requires the cumulative-percentage line to come from actual table calculations (running total, then percent of total) rather than hand-entered values that only look like a Pareto curve.

questions.q: Why does this lesson intentionally not include a finished screenshot of 'the' correct dashboard?
options: Because there are many equally valid layouts and choices, and showing one specific screenshot would present it as the single correct answer rather than a self-directed challenge
Because screenshots are technically impossible to take of a finished Tableau dashboard
Because the challenge has no correct way to complete it
Because Tableau prohibits screenshots of dashboards
questions.explain: Every technique needed already had a real, sourced screenshot in Lessons 74-77. This lesson deliberately withholds a single finished-dashboard image so the challenge stays open-ended rather than becoming 'copy this exact layout.'

questions.q: What confirms a dynamic reference line was built correctly, per this lesson's rubric?
options: Its Value field points at a parameter, and a parameter action actually moves it (e.g., on hover or select)
It is colored a bright, contrasting color
It appears on every worksheet in the workbook
It uses a FIXED LOD expression instead of a parameter
questions.explain: The rubric requires both halves: the reference line's Value field referencing a parameter, AND a parameter action that actually updates that parameter based on user interaction — a parameter alone isn't enough to call it dynamic.
